technical-summary:
AS59 Stage 1 work items 1-5: config-driven composition, replacing import-time construction in the CLI startup path.

foundation/composition (new, domain-blind): distinct ServiceId/ImplementationId NewTypes; a frozen ServiceContribution (service id, implementation id, factory, requires keyed by factory parameter name, optional explicit finalizer); a config schema of exactly two keys (roots, bindings) hosted on the existing load_layered_config three-tier precedence API rather than a new loader; and a builder that indexes contributions, validates the whole binding map, walks only from configured roots, detects cycles reporting participants in order, constructs in dependency order and returns an immutable BuiltGraph.

BuiltGraph's public surface is exactly root(), shutdown() and construction_order. There is no runtime get(): root() returns configured roots only, so a service built as a dependency is unreachable through it. Finalizers run in reverse construction order, a failing finalizer does not abandon the rest, and shutdown is idempotent. Build-time overrides allow fake substitution without touching module state. No implicit default binding: a service with one implementation still requires an explicit binding (VAL-COMPOSE-006).

runtime/bootstrap (new, the composition root and the only reader of bindings): ApplicationHost owns process startup/shutdown and no business logic; builtin_contributions is an explicit list with no scanning or plugin discovery. The graph has a real edge - runtime.application-host depends on foundation.interaction-backend, bound to foundation.cli-interaction, chosen because InteractionBackend is an existing Protocol whose contract already names CLI and MCP elicitation as alternatives. launcher.py's startup block now builds the graph and calls host.start(); argparse and both dispatch registries are unchanged, and harness-status functions are passed as a callable so the runtime.harness import stays deferred.

Eight error codes registered in foundation/error-resolutions.yaml before first use (VAL-COMPOSE-001..007, CON-COMPOSE-001), verified to resolve with the catalogue actually loaded rather than only present in YAML.

49 new tests. Architecture tests enforce by source inspection: foundation composition imports no component/runtime code, composition is domain-blind across all identifiers, the graph exposes no runtime lookup, only the composition root reads bindings, no service imports composition, launcher.py is the sole caller of the composition root, the shipped YAML names no Python paths, and every composition error code is registered.

Validation: full unit suite green under -n auto --dist loadfile except the one documented pre-existing Windows orphan-cleanup failure (AS52); ruff clean; CLI output unchanged. One recorded behaviour difference: the started/exit log records now carry logger name audiagentic.runtime.bootstrap.application_host instead of audiagentic.launcher (field values and ordering unchanged).

Scope explicitly not taken: the queue-manager half of item 6 is deferred on the owner's instruction, reducing item 6 to the already-Protocol-shaped gateway profile registry; the queue manager needs a narrow Protocol extracted first and that is not yet budgeted. AS76 was raised to hold the separate question of whether the nine module-global Registry instances should relate to the composition graph - answered no for unification, deferred for the registry-ownership question until a composed consumer exists.

technical-summary:
Closes AS59 Stage 1 work items 8 (legacy-exemption half) and 9, and re-scopes item 6 on evidence.

Item 6 asked to migrate the queue / Execution Profile resolver into composition. Three candidates were assessed against the tree and all rejected:

- Queue manager: one implementation, no interface, reachable only via 13 module-level free functions with 18 external callers. Already owned by AS63 per the disposition table.
- Gateway profile registry: looked strongest (Protocol, two implementations, 1 read + 2 writes in src) but is not a binding candidate on semantics. None is a meaningful value meaning embedded mode with a documented queue-side fallback; the service host installs and uninstalls it at runtime; reload_profile_registry() hot-swaps it under a lock. A frozen build-time graph cannot express deliberately-absent or hot-swap.
- Session runtime: one implementation so not a binding, a lifetime candidate only, and hits the same free-function injection barrier.

Root cause recorded: agents_gateway_api exposes its entire surface as module-level free functions, so no dependency can be injected without changing signatures. That reshaping belongs to AS60/AS63. Forcing a migration would have produced the hidden global fallback the acceptance criteria forbid.

Added test_only_the_application_host_installs_the_interaction_backend, asserting the one startup path Stage 1 actually migrated has no second caller. The startup paths still called elsewhere (logging.bootstrap from 9 component MCP servers plus component_server, register_harness_status from runtime/harness) are deliberately not asserted, because asserting them would claim a migration that has not happened.

Added the legacy exemption register: every startup path still constructed outside composition, its exemption basis, and its adoption owner (AS63, SH11 Slice B, AS60, AS76, or unassigned for the MCP server process kind). This supplies the implementing step for the previously orphaned acceptance criterion requiring the remaining process kinds to have a recorded adoption owner. Also documents how later factories are contributed - append a ServiceContribution and name it in composition.yaml, with no discovery or plugin lifecycle until two independent contributors exist outside the composition root.

Steps, Validation and Files updated to match delivered scope rather than predicted scope.

Validation: 50 new tests green. Full unit suite run twice under -n auto --dist loadfile; both runs green except the pre-existing Windows orphan-cleanup failure. A second failure (test_partial_registry_repopulates_missing_implementations) appeared in run one only, passed in isolation, and did not recur in run two - the known non-deterministic registry-churn flake tracked by TE02 step 10, not a regression. Ruff clean on all touched files; the 47 remaining src errors are pre-existing in untouched modules.

AS59 Stage 1 is complete and AS60 is unblocked.

technical-summary:
Consumed the role-capabilities plan into agent-sessions, resolving a two-owner conflict on the Role concept (RV886), and recorded AS59's composition granularity rule.

The conflict: AS61's AS59 disposition claimed sole Role ownership while role-capabilities RO01-RO04 defined role and capability contracts. The claim was made in good faith - AS59's Disposition Table states its scope as agent-sessions items only and never surveyed other plans - but arch-standards section 3 requires one owner per durable artifact.

Reading both sides in full showed they were not competing for the same scope. AS61's Do not add list forbids runtime tool-set normalization and tool-policy resolution, and its acceptance criteria defer runtime tool policy to a future owning plan; AS64 states tool/MCP/permission capability matching is out of scope. RO02-RO04 are that deferred layer, not a rival definition. Genuine overlap was confined to RO01, which mixed Role-type design with capability vocabulary.

Resolution: RO01 step 4 (precedence vs agent-profile/workflow-profile/component-profile, previously unowned) absorbed into AS61; RO01 steps 2 and 5 (capability vocabulary, least-capability defaults) into AS77; RO01 step 1 (all-or-nothing exposure inventory) into AS79 as its evidence gate. RO02 to AS77 (capability resolver and immutable launch manifest), RO03 to AS78 (submission and gateway integration), RO04 to AS79 (presets and policy gates). RO01-RO04 set superseded with pointer tables; the role-capabilities active plan is now empty.

Each successor gained constraints absent from its source: AS59 Rule 0 (the resolver is component-internal and never a composition binding), an automated anti-drift check on AS78's resolve-once constraint, AS79 named as the owner of AS78's bounded section-4 compatibility default, and explicit statements that AS77 consumes the PC provider-capability catalogue and AS29's surface-capability authority rather than defining a second capability model.

Also recorded in AS59: Rule 0 as the primary composition criterion - a binding names a component public surface or a foundation capability, never an internal collaborator - which reframes the earlier item 6 finding. The queue manager, session runtime and profile registry were never candidates at any granularity rather than candidates that failed on blast radius. The legacy exemption register's Disposition column now distinguishes boundary from internal, where internal means never in the graph rather than deferred. Expected steady-state binding count is order-tens, tracking boundaries not classes, which is the checkable guard against the graph becoming a container and what keeps a later swap to a real DI engine bounded.

AS59's Disposition Table gained an explicit scope caveat stating it is authority over agent-sessions items only and that a sole owner disposition is not a repo-wide claim - the omission that let the collision go unnoticed. The Composition Track sequence carries AS77-AS79 as a role capability lane hanging off AS61/AS64 rather than extending the spine, since AS62 and AS63 do not depend on it.

AS76 narrowed: the nine module-global Registry instances are component-internal entity catalogues and therefore never composition candidates, so that item is no longer gated on AS59 Stage 1.

A sequencing hazard is recorded on AS77 and AS78: shared-gateway SH12 is a P1 single no-alias cutover renaming the LLM gateway vocabulary across code, events, MCP tools, schemas, docs and tests, and rewrites the same surface AS78 edits. They must not run in parallel.

Removed RO01-RO04 from the legacy section-debt baseline in tests/unit/planning/test_plan_set_integrity.py - debt paid rather than moved, since AS77-AS79 carry acceptance criteria. Plan-set integrity green.
user-summary-candidate: Consolidated the agent-role planning work into a single sequence so role definition, capability resolution, and rollout each have one owner instead of two overlapping plans.
